title: Multiple Type Params
concept: Functions and types can have multiple type parameters — T and U, K and V — each independent and optionally constrained separately.
why: Real-world abstractions often need multiple independent types: a Map needs K and V, a Result needs T and E, a Pair needs T and U.
syntax_ref:
fn name[T, U](a: T, b: U) -> ReturnType { /* body */ }
pub type Name[K: Constraint, V] = { key: K; value: V; }
tips: Use conventional names: T and U for general types, K and V for key-value pairs, E for error
Only add as many type params as needed — don't add unused params
Each type param can have its own constraints (or none)
The order of type params matters: Result[T, E] has a different meaning than Result[E, T]
common_mistakes: Adding unnecessary type params — if two params are always the same type, use one
Forgetting constraints on one param when the other has them
Mixing up parameter order when calling: zip[Int, Str] vs zip[Str, Int]
